article.Citation/Title: Johnson MW, Naude, G. P., Hendricks, P. S., & Garcia-Romeu, A. (2026). Psilocybin or nicotine patch for smoking cessation: A pilot randomized clinical trial. JAMA Network Open.
article.InterventionDescription: Single 30 mg/70 kg oral psilocybin dose during a supervised ~8-9 hour session (eyeshades, music) plus 13-week manualized CBT; comparator arm received 8-10 weeks nicotine patch plus CBT.

article.Outcome: A priori primary outcome is 6-month biochemically verified prolonged smoking abstinence; the reported effect size for the primary between-group comparison is OR = 6.12 (95% CI, 1.99-23.26; P = .003) from binary logistic regression, stated in the Abstract and the 'Smoking Cessation Outcomes' section of Results. Not the largest available statistic (7-day point-prevalence OR = 3.30 is secondary; the exploratory zero-inflated mixed model's incidence rate ratio is a tertiary/exploratory analysis) — Outcome reflects the designated primary endpoint per the precedence rule.
article.SD: 95% CI, 1.99-23.26 is the dispersion measure the article pairs directly with the primary OR of 6.12 (Abstract; Results).
article.PVal: P = .003 is reported immediately alongside the primary OR of 6.12 in the Abstract and Results.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: Intention-to-treat analysis for the primary 6-month prolonged-abstinence outcome included all N = 82 randomized participants (42 psilocybin, 40 nicotine patch); participants who discontinued or were lost to follow-up were counted as nonabstinent rather than excluded, so 82 (not the 68 who completed the 6-month visit) is the denominator over which the primary OR was computed (Methods, 'Statistical Analysis'; Results).

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: All 14 elements are explicitly described. Sample-size/power counts as described (not merely present) because the article explicitly states sample size was driven by funding rather than a statistical power calculation. Blinding counts as described because the article explicitly states participants and investigators were unblinded, satisfying the 'described as absent' clause.

article.Power: Coded 1 because the article explicitly discusses the absence of a formal a priori power calculation ('Sample size was informed by financial rather than statistical considerations because of limited data on effect size from prior research'), which the coding rule treats as 'discussed' even without a completed calculation (Methods).
article.Retention (%): 82.9 = 68/82 (completers of the 6-month primary follow-up / total randomized N), matching the article's directly stated figure ('68 [82.9%] completing the 6-month follow-up'). Randomized N used as denominator per the randomized-study convention.
article.ConfoundYN: Coded 1 because (a) the primary logistic-regression models were run without covariates on the stated basis of 'highly comparable group baseline characteristics' (an explicit baseline-balance justification), (b) an exploratory analysis specifically tested whether prior lifetime psychedelic use — a plausible confounder — was associated with outcome (it was not), and (c) baseline CPD was included as a covariate in the exploratory mixed-effects model of daily cigarette use.
article.BaseStatus: Coded 'Moderate': mean FTCD (Fagerstrom Test for Cigarette Dependence) was 4.6-4.7 (borderline low-to-moderate on the 0-10 scale) and mean CPD was ~15.7/day with a median of 6 prior failed quit attempts — indicating an established, moderately dependent smoking population rather than a minimally dependent or an extreme/heaviest-use (severe) sample.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: 11.0 = 100 - 89.0% White = 3.7% Black/African American + 4.9% East/Southeast Asian + 2.4% multiracial (Results, total-sample race breakdown, N = 82).
article.SocioeconomicStatusYN: Coded 0: the article reports educational attainment (bachelor's degree or higher) but no income, low-income eligibility criterion, or public-insurance data, so low-SES inclusion is not explicitly described.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: Country is the United States — Johns Hopkins Bayview Medical Center, Baltimore, Maryland (Methods).
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Coded 0: participants were self-selected volunteers responding to ads seeking interest in a 'novel research approach' to quitting; 64.6% reported prior psychedelic use vs 13.8% nationally, and the sample was more educated/higher-intelligence than the general smoking population. Authors explicitly flag this as a recruitment-bias/generalizability limitation (Discussion, 'Limitations').
article.PrimaryCare: Coded 0: the trial was conducted entirely within a specialty academic-medical-center research clinic (Johns Hopkins Bayview); no primary-care setting or provider involvement is described.
article.MentalHealthChangeMeasured: Coded 0: depression and anxiety appear only as adverse-event categories in the AE table (Table 2), not as outcomes assessed via a validated mental-health instrument (e.g., no PHQ-9/GAD-7 or similar scale is reported as a study outcome).
article.Implementation Outcome: Coded 0: facilitator-assignment and contact-time data are reported descriptively (eTables 1 and 3) but no formal feasibility/acceptability/fidelity/reach/adoption/sustainability outcome is defined or measured.
article.ReductionMeasured: Coded 1: mean post-target-quit-date cigarettes-per-day, modeled via generalized linear mixed-effects models, is reported as a distinct exploratory outcome separate from the binary abstinence/cessation endpoints (Results, 'Statistical Analysis' and 'Smoking Cessation Outcomes').
article.RelapseMeasured: Coded 1, non-obvious call: the article does not use the word 'relapse,' but Figure 3 and the accompanying text report biochemically verified abstinence status longitudinally at weeks 2, 4, 6, 8, 13, and 26, which functionally tracks return-to-smoking over time in participants who had achieved abstinence.
article.Followup in months: 6 months is the longest follow-up horizon with outcome data reported in this article (a priori primary endpoint). The article states 12-month follow-up data exist but 'will be published separately,' so 12-month results are not extractable from this text.
article.NumDistinctAEs: Coded 'Not numbered' rather than an integer. Table 2 is explicitly restricted to 'adverse events reported in >=2 participants during the trial' and lists 20 named AE types with psilocybin-arm counts, but the article states a full listing (including presumably singleton AEs affecting only 1 participant) is in eTable 2 of Supplement 2, which is not part of the converted text available for this extraction. The 20-type count from Table 2 is therefore a floor, not the true total, so it is coded 'Not numbered' per the non-fabrication rule. Additionally, the extracted Table 2 markdown is itself garbled/column-shifted around the 'Elevated blood pressure' row, reinforcing that a confident integer total cannot be asserted.
article.AE_denominator: Coded 82 (total randomized N), matching the headline statement '70 participants (85.4%) reported an AE' (70/82 = 85.4%, confirming this denominator). Note: the per-event breakdown in Table 2 uses a narrower population (n = 40 psilocybin-arm and n = 40 nicotine-patch-arm participants who received the study intervention, per footnote b, N = 80 total, excluding 2 psilocybin-randomized participants who did not receive the drug). 82 is used here as the article's overall/primary safety-population denominator; the per-event ae_events NAffected values are drawn from the n = 40 psilocybin-arm column specifically (noted in each event's Description).
article.ArmScope: Coded 'pooled' at the article level because Table 2 as designed reports AE values for both the psilocybin arm and the nicotine-patch (comparator) arm side by side, mixing exposed and comparator participants; the headline 70/82 AE-prevalence figure likewise spans both arms. Individual ae_events NAffected values in this extraction come from the psilocybin-arm column specifically (the only column reliably parseable from the garbled table), which is flagged in each event's Description.
article.WorstSeverity: Coded 'Moderate': the article states no serious AEs occurred, but one psilocybin-administration case of elevated blood pressure required active pharmacological intervention (0.4 mg sublingual nitroglycerin), which meets the rubric's Moderate band (intervention required, no FDA seriousness criterion met, no further sequelae). No event in the article meets an FDA seriousness criterion or is author-labeled an SAE, so no event reaches Severe.

config_proposal.note: Directly reported OR = 6.12 (95% CI, 1.99-23.26; P = .003) from binary logistic regression for the a priori primary outcome (6-month biochemically verified prolonged abstinence), ITT N = 82. Independently recomputed from the reported 2x2 cell counts (17/42 psilocybin abstinent vs 4/40 nicotine-patch abstinent: OR = (17x36)/(25x4) = 6.12), which matches the reported value exactly, supporting a clean conversion with no assumption required.
